title: Docker & Kubernetes: Ship with Confidence
tagline: Package a real API into a lean, secure image and run it on Kubernetes without 3 a.m. surprises.
description: Containers are how most software ships in 2026, and Kubernetes is where much of it runs. This course takes one small service, notes-api (Node.js and Postgres), from a laptop to a cluster. You write the Dockerfile, shrink and harden the image, wire up a local stack with Docker Compose, then deploy, scale, update and roll back on Kubernetes.

Your instructor is Amara Diallo, a cloud architect at Skylane who carries the pager for production clusters. Every recommendation here is tied to an incident it prevents: the cache that took builds from forty seconds to eight minutes, the secret baked into a public image, the rollout that sent traffic to Pods that weren't ready. You learn the defaults that keep services boring.
audience: Developers who can build a small web API and now need to package, run and operate it with containers.
prerequisites: Comfort with the command line, Git and one backend language; Node.js is used in examples.
learnItems: Write fast, cache-friendly Dockerfiles with multi-stage builds
Ship small, non-root images pinned by digest and scanned for CVEs
Run an app and its database locally with Docker Compose
Deploy with Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps and Secrets
Add probes, resource requests and autoscaling that hold up under load
Roll out, roll back and debug a broken release with kubectl and Helm
